outline_section.section_title: Interpreting Complex-Conjugate Pole Pairs on a Pole-Zero Plot
outline_section.learning_goal: Read a pole-zero plot to identify the conjugate pair and interpret decay/growth and oscillation directly from plotted coordinates.

image_policy.image_description_seed: Pole-zero plot in the s-plane showing axes and a highlighted conjugate pair at mirrored points above/below the real axis.
visual_elements: two highlighted complex poles symmetric about real axis
image_policy.image_generation_notes: Use a clean pole-zero diagram where learners must visually extract coordinates; do not encode answer choices as images.

question_policy.answer_format: five options combining identified pair coordinates and behavioral interpretation
question_policy.practice_question_model: From a given pole-zero plot, identify the highlighted conjugate pair and choose its correct decay/growth and oscillation interpretation.
distractor_plan: Include distractors that confuse real and imaginary coordinates.
Include distractors that choose a mirrored point from a different pair.
Include distractors that swap stability classification while keeping the same frequency.
Include distractors that report frequency as one component of pair coordinates instead of magnitude.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: On the provided pole-zero plot, the highlighted pair is at $(-2\pm j4)$. State the corresponding response form and behavior.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Read coordinates from the plot, convert to $-2\pm j4$, and explain decaying oscillatory behavior.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: This step transfers the same interpretation language to the visual domain and makes the final move for the topic.
solution_step_plan: Identify the highlighted conjugate pair from the plot symmetry.
Compute real-part magnitude and sign for decay/growth.
Compute frequency from $|\omega|=4$ and report combined interpretation.
practice_variation_axes: Vary pair positions across left and right half-planes.
Vary imaginary magnitude while keeping real part fixed.
Introduce additional poles/zeros so the task requires selecting the target pair first.

outline_section.handoff_notes: Treat this as the image-in-question transition; both example and practice must force coordinate extraction from the same visual data source.

prompt_blocks.text: On the provided pole-zero plot, which option correctly identifies the highlighted pair and its response behavior?
Choose the option that matches both the pole coordinates and the decay/growth and oscillation interpretation.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The highlighted points are mirror images across the real axis, so the pair is $s=-3\pm j2$.
The real part is negative, so the envelope decays. The imaginary magnitude is $2$, so the response oscillates at $2\,\mathrm{rad/s}$.
